tickets.background:
### Goal
Establish the siprs crate as a compilable Rust crate with a defined module hierarchy (lib.rs + mod.rs), documented identity (non-purpose, Tauri boundary, glossary), versioning policy enforcement via compile-time constants, and a published M20 priority roadmap reference. All meta/documentation items that form the crate's identity and governance must be in place.

### Purpose
Without these foundations, the crate lacks: 1) A compilable module structure (no lib.rs = uncompilable), 2) Versioning policy enforcement (breaking change rules, semver contract), 3) Published identity (what the crate does, doesn't do, and how it integrates with Tauri), 4) Shared vocabulary (Client, Account, Call, etc. — essential for all subsequent tickets), 5) Implementation priority visibility (M20 map shows the full P0-P3 roadmap).

### Motivation
Phase P0 starts here because every subsequent ticket (P0-2, P0-3, ..., P3-X) depends on the crate being compilable and having documented boundaries. 39 stub files are structurally orphaned with no module tree. No implementation can proceed until lib.rs and the module hierarchy exist.

### Constraints
- Zero new runtime dependencies (compile-time constants only; env!() macros are free from Cargo.toml)
- Must not break existing test expectations (tests/versioning_policy_test.rs asserts 8 function signatures reachable through siprs::api::versioning_policy::*)
- #[non_exhaustive] on SipEventPayload must be structural (enum-level attribute, checked at compile time), not doc-level prose
- Crate-level documentation must use #[doc = "..."] or inner line comments (#![doc = "..."]), not a separate documentation-only crate
- No Tauri dependency — crate must remain pure Rust, no tauri::ipc or JavaScript FFI
- M20 priority map is a reference table documenting the roadmap, not an implementation commitment
- PJSIP version is a placeholder string until FFI layer (P3 tickets); non_exhaustive assertion must work without SipEventPayload being fully implemented

testExceptions: Exception 1 — Item: MSRV runtime detection via compiling a temp crate and parsing its Cargo.toml at runtime. Reason: MSRV is a compile-time constant set in Cargo.toml rust-version field ("1.95"); runtime detection of own crate MSRV is impossible because the crate is already compiled — runtime code cannot re-read its own Cargo.toml without filesystem access, which breaks determinism and adds unnecessary API surface (filesystem I/O in a pure configuration module). This is NOT a "deterministic yet untestable" defect: the compile-time constant env!("CARGO_PKG_RUST_VERSION") is verified at build time by cargo, and the unit test confirms the constant propagates correctly by asserting msrv() == env!("CARGO_PKG_RUST_VERSION") — the correctness boundary is the cargo build toolchain, not runtime code logic

Exception 2 — Item: PJSIP version runtime detection via FFI (pj_get_version()). Reason: PJSIP library is not yet linked (FFI layer is P3 tickets — N0040, N0031); pjsip_version() returns a compile-time placeholder string ("targeting PJSIP 2.x") until FFI bindings exist. This IS a "deterministic yet temporarily untestable" situation by design: the placeholder is intentional and documented as [::STUB::]. Alternative verification: integration test confirms the placeholder constant value via assert!(!pjsip_version().is_empty()); when PJSIP FFI is linked (P3 tickets), upgrade to call pj_get_version() via FFI and remove this exception entry

Exception 3 — Item: cargo doc --no-deps rendering correctness of crate-level doc sections (non-purpose, Tauri boundary, glossary, M20 map). Reason: Doc comments (#[doc = "..."]) are rendered by rustdoc, a separate toolchain invocation — there is no runtime assertion mechanism for doc content beyond doc-tests (which test code examples inside docs, not the prose itself). This is NOT a "deterministic yet untestable" defect: doc content correctness is a documentation review concern, not a code correctness concern. tickets.invariants:
- 【Normal establishment】All compile-time version constants (crate_version, msrv, pjsip_version) must resolve at compile time via env!() or static &'static str literals; module declarations (lib.rs + mod.rs) must be syntactically valid for cargo check to succeed; #[doc = "..."] attributes must be valid Rust syntax and not break compilation
- 【Invariant on error】Since all values are compile-time constants (no fallible runtime operations), there is no error path at runtime; a compile-time failure (via env!() on missing env var) is a hard error that blocks compilation entirely — no silent fallback, no default value substitution is permitted
- 【Internal state invariant】The module has zero internal mutable state — all functions return compile-time constants; no static mut or thread_local; all functions are pure (same input → same output) and automatically Send + Sync via &'static str / &'static [&'static str] / bool return types
- 【Boundary invariant】semver_breaking_change_allowance() returns true iff Cargo.toml version major == "0" (version < 1.0.0); msrv_semver_range() output must start with ">=" (valid semver::VersionReq prefix); supported_os_list() must return at least 1 entry (OS platform cannot be empty)
tickets.instrumentation:
- 【Logging】No runtime logging needed — all functions return compile-time constants; versioning_policy_description() is already doc-level prose, not log output; crate-level doc (#[doc = "..."]) is rendered by rustdoc, not printed at runtime
- 【Metrics】No runtime metrics — zero mutable state, zero performance-sensitive operations; version constants are evaluated once at compile time with zero runtime cost
- 【Error tracking】No runtime error path exists — compile-time failures (missing env!() variable) are caught by cargo build and reported as clear compiler errors; no error recovery logic needed
- 【Health check】No runtime health check needed — the module has no internal state, no I/O, no async operations; health is trivially "available" if the crate compiles
